actions.reader_question: How much will my Part D premium go up in 2027, and what do I do before December 7? [PAA 1/6 on-topic, 5/6 off-topic: RX plan, losing Medicare, free plan at 65, Star Ratings, MA cancellations (keyword-intent flag); ac 4 of 21 shown: premium / cost / how-much / is-increasing completions (seniors, rates, pdf variants not counted)]
actions.answer: If you keep a stand-alone drug plan, KFF projects the average premium rises from $34 to $51 a month in 2027, about $204 more a year; KFF reports no zero-premium stand-alone plans are available in 2027 and says people facing large increases need to act to avoid paying significantly more, with open enrollment running through December 7. (figure with its action)

newPageBriefs.takeaway: A stand-alone enrollee who keeps the same plan faces the average $17 a month ($204 a year) KFF projects, and KFF says action is needed with open enrollment through December 7. Applies to stand-alone plan enrollees, not Extra Help recipients ($0 premium per Medicare.gov) or Medicare Advantage with drug coverage ($9 average). Evidence basis: reported (KFF, CMS, Medicare.gov). Changes if the plan's own 2027 premium is flat or a $700-deductible low-premium plan costs more in total. Next step: use Medicare Plan Finder to compare plans before December 7.
